thread.title: Stock Market Update: Futures Point to Flattish Open Ahead of Apple iPhone Unveiling

title: Stock Market Update: Futures Point to Flattish Open Ahead of Apple iPhone Unveiling
text:
Futures Point to Flattish Open Ahead of Apple iPhone Unveiling 12-Sep-18 07:58 ET Market is Closed [BRIEFING.COM] S&P futures vs fair value: -1.50. Nasdaq futures vs fair value: +2.00.
Equity futures are pointing towards a flattish open following back-to-back victories for Wall Street. The S&P 500 futures are two points below fair value.
Apple (AAPL), the world's largest tech company, will hold its annual product showcase this afternoon at 1:00 PM ET, where it will unveil its latest iPhone lineup, new Apple Watches, and new Airpods. The new high-end iPhone, which will likely be called the iPhone X Plus or Max, is expected to have a price tag somewhere between $1049 and $1099 vs the current base price of $999 for the iPhone X.
However, before that, investors will receive the Producer Price Index for August (Briefing.com consensus +0.2%), which will be released at 8:30 AM ET. The weekly MBA Mortgage Applications Index was released earlier this morning, showing a decline of 1.8% vs last week's downtick of 0.1%. The Fed's Beige Book will cross the wires at 2:00 PM ET.
Hurricane Florence has continued moving towards the East Coast, where it is expected to make landfall either late Thursday or early Friday. The storm has helped boost crude prices, with WTI crude futures up 1.0% at $69.95/bbl. Also helping underpin crude prices is Thursday's weekly inventory report from the API, which showed that stockpiles declined by 8.6 million barrels. The official government figures will be released at 10:30 AM ET.
Looking at other markets, U.S. Treasuries have rebounded after falling on Tuesday, pushing yields lower across the curve, with the benchmark 10-yr yield down two basis points at 2.96%. Meanwhile, the U.S. Dollar Index is up 0.2% at 95.19, gold is down 0.3% at $1199.20, and the CBOE Volatility Index is up 0.5% at 13.28.
In U.S. corporate news: Apple (AAPL 224.80, +0.95): +0.4% ahead of today's iPhone launch event -- which will kick off at 1:00 PM ET. Gilead Sciences (GILD 74.69, +2.46): +3.4% after the company and Galapagos NV (GLPG 118.29, +15.55, +15.1%) announced positive trial results for a combined arthritis treatment. Micron (MU 42.18, -1.42): -3.3% after being downgraded to 'Neutral' from 'Buy' at Goldman.
Reviewing overnight developments: Equity indices in the Asia-Pacific region ended the midweek session on a mixed note. Japan's Nikkei -0.2%, Hong Kong's Hang Seng -0.3%, China's Shanghai Composite -0.3%, India's Sensex +0.8%. In economic data: China's August New Loans CNY1.28 trillion (expected CNY1.30 trillion; last CNY1.45 trillion). August M2 Money Stock +8.2% year-over-year (expected 8.5%; last 8.5%). August Outstanding Loan Growth +13.2% year-over-year, as expected (last 13.2%) Japan's Q3 BSI Large Manufacturing Conditions 6.5 (expected 8.0; last -3.2) Australia's September Westpac Consumer Sentiment -3.0% (last -2.3%) Singapore's July Retail Sales -2.9% month-over-month (last 1.3%); -2.6% year-over-year (last 2.2%) South Korea's August Unemployment Rate 4.2% (last 3.8%) and M2 Money Supply +6.2% (last 6.6%) In news: Hong Kong's Hang Seng recorded its sixth consecutive decline and is now down 21.3% from its January high. Japan's Prime Minister Shinzo Abe met with China's President Xi Jinping at Russia's Eastern Economic Forum. The two leaders agreed to deepen cooperation between the two countries and work toward the first visit by a Japanese prime minister to Beijing since 2011. South Korea's unemployment rate rose to its highest level in more than eight years. Major European indices trade near their flat lines while France's CAC (+0.3%) outperforms. UK's FTSE +0.1%, Germany's DAX +0.1%. In economic data: Eurozone July Industrial Production -0.8% month-over-month (expected -0.5%; last -0.8%); -0.1% year-over-year (expected 1.0%; last 2.3%) Italy's July Industrial Production -1.8% month-over-month (expected -0.4%; last 0.3%); -1.3% year-over-year (expected 1.4%; last 1.4%) Spain's August CPI +0.1% month-over-month (expected 0.2%; last 0.2%); +2.2% year-over-year, as expected (last 2.2%) In news: The approval rating of French President Emmanuel Macron has declined to 25.0%, according to a poll conducted by Ipsos. The European Central Bank will reportedly lower its growth outlook while keeping inflation expectations unchanged. The ECB will release its latest policy statement tomorrow at 7:45 ET. European Commission President Jean-Claude Juncker expressed desire to work towards a satisfactory Brexit deal. The European Parliament has censured Hungary for threatening EU values.
